records.title: Suspension Bushing Premature Wear
records.description: The front and rear suspension bushings wear prematurely due to the stiff suspension setup and lightweight construction. Track use accelerates wear significantly, causing clunks and wandering.
records.solution: Replace worn bushings with polyurethane or spherical upgrades for improved longevity. Perform a full alignment after bushing replacement. Track-focused owners should inspect bushings every 10,000 miles.

records.title: TCT Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder
records.description: The Alfa TCT (Twin Clutch Transmission) develops shudder and hesitation at low speeds, particularly during parking maneuvers and stop-and-go traffic. The dry dual-clutch design wears faster under frequent low-speed use.
records.solution: Perform a TCT clutch adaptation reset using Alfa Romeo diagnostic software (WiTech). If shudder persists after adaptation, the clutch pack assembly requires replacement.

records.title: Front Brake Squeal and Dust
records.description: The front brakes produce excessive squeal during light braking and generate heavy brake dust. The aggressive OEM pad compound prioritizes stopping power over noise and dust characteristics.
records.solution: Replace the OEM brake pads with a ceramic compound alternative for reduced noise and dust. Clean and lubricate the caliper slide pins and apply anti-squeal shims. The Quadrifoglio Brembo calipers need specific QV pads.
symptoms: Excessive black brake dust on wheels

records.title: Contaminated Brake/Clutch Fluid (Reduced Braking)
records.description: A batch of Giulias and Stelvios left the assembly plant with brake and clutch fluid contaminated by an incompatible mineral oil. The contamination can swell seals and degrade braking performance, in some cases producing system failure with little warning. NHTSA/Alfa identified roughly 307 affected vehicles built in a specific window.
records.solution: Under the recall, dealers inspect the braking system and replace the affected brake/clutch fluid and components as necessary, free of charge. Out of warranty, a full brake fluid flush with the correct DOT-spec fluid and seal inspection is the remedy.

records.title: Electrical Faults from Water Intrusion / BCM Failure
records.description: Water enters the cowl/firewall area (failed bulkhead gasket, detached fresh-air vent, or clogged A/C evaporator drain) and drips onto the Body Control Module and wiring loom in the passenger footwell. The resulting corrosion and shorts cause wide-ranging, intermittent electrical failures. Owners have reported headlights, brake lights, turn signals, and driver-assist systems all cutting out at speed, plus dead batteries and warning-light storms.
records.solution: Fix the water-intrusion source first (reseal bulkhead gasket, reattach fresh-air vent, clear the A/C drain) before replacing electronics. A water-damaged BCM must be replaced and re-programmed with a proxy alignment (not plug-and-play); used modules often require harness re-pinning. Dry and inspect the footwell wiring loom.
symptoms: Lights or signals failing while driving

records.title: Infotainment System Random Reboots
records.description: The Uconnect infotainment system reboots randomly during driving, losing navigation, audio, and phone connectivity. The system can take 30-60 seconds to restart, leaving the driver without backup camera or climate controls.
records.solution: Update the Uconnect software to the latest version. Perform a factory reset if issues persist. Some units require hardware replacement of the head unit.

records.title: Interior/Cabin Water Leaks (Cowl, Bulkhead, A/C Drain)
records.description: Beyond its electrical consequences, the Giulia has a recurring water-leak problem where rain or car-wash water enters via the cowl under the windshield, a failed firewall/bulkhead seal, or a clogged A/C evaporator drain, soaking the passenger footwell carpet. Dealers report seeing the detached fresh-air vent and bulkhead leak repeatedly. Standing water promotes mold, odor, and downstream electronics corrosion.
records.solution: Identify the source: reseal the bulkhead gasket, reattach the fresh-air inlet vent, clear or extend the A/C evaporator drain tube, and confirm cowl drains are unobstructed. Dry the carpet and underlayment thoroughly and inspect any footwell electronics for water damage.
symptoms: Wet passenger or driver footwell carpet
Water dripping from under the dash
Leaks after rain or car wash

records.title: Jerky / Hunting Transmission at Low Speed (ZF 8-Speed)
records.description: The ZF 8-speed automatic, combined with throttle-by-wire and brake-by-wire, can shift harshly or hunt between gears (commonly around 3rd-4th) at low speed and light throttle, and jerk when transitioning off the auto stop-start neutral state. The behavior is exaggerated in Dynamic (D) mode where shift mapping is intentionally aggressive, and worsens when the powertrain is cold.
records.solution: Have the dealer open a case to apply ECM/TCM software updates and reprogramming, which smooths shift quality for many owners. As a workaround, disable auto stop-start and use Normal/All-Weather modes for low-speed driving; ensure the car is fully warmed up. Verify transmission fluid level/condition if symptoms persist.
symptoms: Jerking back and forth at low speed

records.title: Low-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure (Sudden Power Loss)
records.description: The in-tank low-pressure fuel pump assembly can warp/degrade from underhood and operating heat, reducing or stopping fuel flow to the engine. This causes engine fuel starvation, leading to stalling or a sudden loss of motive power (LOMP) while driving, often without warning. NHTSA opened preliminary evaluation PE24-003 and the issue escalated to a full recall (25V586) covering roughly 53,849 Giulia and Stelvio vehicles; Stellantis acknowledged 437+ North American complaints and five crashes in Europe.
records.solution: Under recall 25V586, dealers replace the fuel delivery module (fuel pump assembly) free of charge. Owners experiencing stalling, hard starts, or P0087 low fuel rail pressure codes should have the fuel pump tested for pressure dropout and replaced. Out of warranty, fuel pump module replacement typically runs in the listed range.

records.title: Parasitic Battery Drain / IBS & Stop-Start Faults
records.description: Owners frequently report the 12V battery draining when the car sits for several days, often traced to modules not sleeping properly, a faulty Intelligent Battery Sensor (IBS), or BCM-related charging logic. Symptoms include battery warning lights after 4-5 days of inactivity, stop-start system failures, and corroded/leaking batteries. Measured parasitic draw stays elevated (250mA+) instead of dropping to a low sleep current.
records.solution: Replace a faulty Intelligent Battery Sensor (IBS) with the revised part, which has resolved intermittent drain for many owners. Address any BCM water damage and apply available software updates to correct charging/sleep logic; verify with a parasitic-draw test and replace the battery if internally damaged.
symptoms: Battery dead after sitting a few days

records.title: Rearview Camera Blank/Inverted Image (Infotainment Recall)
records.description: A printed-circuit-board defect and software-stability fault in the Marelli-supplied infotainment/radio unit can cause the rearview camera to display a blank, black, blue, or inverted image when reverse is selected, reducing rear visibility. This led to NHTSA recall 25V667 covering 62,910 Giulia and Stelvio vehicles. Owners also report the infotainment screen freezing or scrambling more generally.
records.solution: Under recall 25V667, dealers inspect and replace the radio/head unit as necessary and update the rearview-camera software, free of charge. For general freezes, owners report a long-press on the volume knob can reboot the unit; vehicles built after March 2025 already have the updated hardware/software.
symptoms: Blank, black, blue, or inverted rearview camera image

records.title: Low-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure Causing Stall (Recall 25V-586)
records.description: 2017+ Giulias can experience sudden engine stall or no-start due to a defective low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel delivery module. The pump's internal commutator wears prematurely and loses contact, cutting fuel supply at any speed. NHTSA recall 25V-586 (Stellantis campaign 93C) covers free replacement. Symptoms include stalling at idle, no-start hot, and intermittent fuel pump prime noise from the rear of the vehicle. Failures cluster at 30,000-80,000 miles.
records.solution: Have the ECM and wiring harness inspected at an Alfa Romeo dealer. FCA has issued TSB 18-024-17 REV.A addressing the wiring harness routing. ECM replacement with updated software may be required.

citations.title: Alfa Romeo Giulia Stall Complaints

records.title: Timing Chain Rattle / Oil Pump Bolt Loosening (2.0T)
records.description: On the 2.0L turbo four-cylinder, owners report a metallic rattle at cold/hot start, attributed to the timing chain tensioner waiting for oil pressure or, in some cases, a loose wastegate actuator. More seriously, early 2017-2018 engines had an oil pump mounting bolt that could loosen, dropping oil pressure and accelerating chain/actuator wear; some owners found metal particles in the oil. Alfa updated the oil pump on 2019/2020+ engines.
records.solution: Diagnose the rattle source: tighten/replace the wastegate actuator if loose, or replace the timing chain assembly and camshaft actuators (variable valve timing solenoids) if the chain has stretched. For affected early engines, inspect/re-torque or replace the oil pump with the updated part. Maintain shorter oil-change intervals (around 6,000 miles) with correct-spec oil.
symptoms: Rattle when parking a hot engine

records.title: Q4 AWD Transfer Case Jolting and Resonance Rumble
records.description: The Giulia Q4 AWD system can develop two related transfer case symptoms with age: a perceptible jolt or slip during light-throttle acceleration in 2nd-3rd gear (output-shaft clutch wear) and a resonant low-frequency rumble at highway speed around 4th-5th gear (worn output bearings). Both are exacerbated by infrequent transfer-case fluid changes. The original 'whining during low-speed turns' description was incorrect — that pattern matches differential wear, not the Q4 transfer case.
records.solution: Drain and refill the transfer case with the correct Alfa Romeo-specified fluid. If noise persists, the transfer case clutch pack assembly needs replacement. FCA extended warranty coverage for some VINs.

records.title: Turbo Coolant Line Leak
records.description: The turbocharger coolant supply and return lines develop leaks at the crimped fittings, causing coolant loss and potential overheating. The plastic quick-connect fittings become brittle from heat cycling.
records.solution: Replace the turbo coolant lines with updated Mopar parts that use improved fittings. Check the coolant level and top off with the correct FCA MS-90032 coolant. Pressure test the system after repair.

records.title: Infotainment System Crash and Black Screen
records.description: The Uconnect infotainment system crashes to a black screen during use, requiring a manual reboot. The issue affects navigation, climate controls, and the backup camera display during the outage.
records.solution: Update the Uconnect software to the latest firmware version. Perform a master reset from the settings menu. If the issue recurs, the head unit hardware may need replacement under warranty.

citations.title: Alfa Romeo Stelvio Infotainment Black Screen

records.title: Low-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure Causing Stall (Recall 25V-667)
records.description: 2018+ Stelvios can experience sudden engine stall or no-start due to a defective low-pressure fuel pump inside the fuel delivery module — same defect as the Giulia, same supplier, same NHTSA timeline. The pump's internal commutator wears prematurely and loses contact, cutting fuel supply at any speed. NHTSA recall 25V-667 (Stellantis campaign 93C) covers free replacement. Failures cluster at 30,000-80,000 miles; stalls reported at highway speed make this safety-critical until repaired.
records.solution: Inspect and repair the ECM harness per FCA TSB 18-024-17 REV.A. Clean and reseal all engine bay ground points. ECM replacement with updated calibration may be needed for persistent cases.

citations.title: Alfa Romeo Stelvio Stall Complaints

records.title: Panoramic Sunroof Rattle and Wind Noise
records.description: The panoramic sunroof develops rattling noises over rough roads and wind noise at highway speeds. The sunroof seal and guide rails are the primary sources of the noise.
records.solution: Adjust the sunroof alignment via the adjustment bolts on the guide rails. Replace the weatherstrip seal if it is compressed or damaged. Apply felt tape to contact points between the glass and frame.

citations.title: Alfa Romeo Stelvio Sunroof Rattle Solutions

records.title: Transfer Case Fluid Leak
records.description: The Q4 AWD transfer case develops fluid leaks from the output shaft seal or housing gasket, resulting in low fluid levels and potential transfer case damage. The leak is often slow and goes unnoticed until noise develops.
records.solution: Replace the leaking transfer case seal or gasket. Refill with the correct Alfa Romeo transfer case fluid. Inspect the transfer case internals for damage if the fluid level was critically low.
symptoms: Fluid drip under center of vehicle

citations.title: Alfa Romeo Stelvio Transfer Case Leak Reports

records.title: Turbo Oil Line Leak
records.description: The turbocharger oil feed and return lines develop leaks at the banjo bolt fittings, causing oil drips onto the exhaust manifold and a burning oil smell. The copper crush washers at the fittings lose their seal over heat cycles.
records.solution: Replace the turbo oil line banjo bolt crush washers with new copper washers. Torque to specification (25 Nm). If the oil line itself is damaged, replace with the updated Mopar part number.

citations.title: Alfa Romeo Stelvio Turbo Oil Leak Reports

records.title: Infotainment Software Bugs
records.description: The new-generation infotainment system has multiple software bugs including frozen touchscreen, incorrect range estimates, and failure to connect to smartphone apps. Over-the-air updates have addressed some but not all issues.
records.solution: Install all available OTA updates. Perform a system reset by holding the power button for 15 seconds. Visit the dealer for a full software reflash if OTA updates do not resolve the issue.

records.title: PHEV Charging System Issues
records.description: The plug-in hybrid charging system can fail to initiate or complete charging sessions, with errors related to the onboard charger module. Scheduled charging sometimes does not activate at the programmed time.
records.solution: Reset the charging schedule in the vehicle settings. Update the PHEV control module software at the dealer. If the onboard charger module has failed, it requires replacement.
